title: Suffix Hit Halting Result
statement: Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let $	ext{mode}$ be a Boolean flag, let $f$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words, let $h$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of $14$ registers. Suppose every register value is at most $B$. Starting in the suffix-hit state with register vector $v$ and no answer recorded, the machine halts with answer true if $	ext{mode}$ is true, and otherwise with the bit of $h$ at position $v_0$, using false when that position is beyond the end; every configuration before halting satisfies the program's step-validity condition and has all register values at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words
$v$ assigns natural values to the 14 registers
Every register value is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be a Boolean flag, let $f$ map bit
strings to bit strings, let $h$ be a bit string, and let $v$ assign a natural number to
each of the 14 registers, with every register value at most $B$. Starting in the
suffix-hit state, the specified counter machine halts with answer true if
$\mathrm{mode}$ is true, and otherwise with the bit of $h$ at the position in register
$0$, using false if that position is beyond the end. The machine's step-validity
condition holds and every register remains at most $B$ throughout the run.
